scenario.summary: A multi-stage ClickFix campaign uses sponsored Google search results for 'Amazon Business' to lead victims to fake login pages and CAPTCHAs that trigger pastejacked commands. These commands abuse the 'finger' utility to download a convoluted sequence of loaders, including IronPython and Node.js, which ultimately deliver Doina malware and Lumma Stealer via process hollowing.

meta.rationale: Start with DNS resolutions to the lure domains, then look for any finger activity. Focus on Windows and macOS endpoints as the finger utility is a default binary on both platforms.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has lured a user to a spoofed Amazon page and pastejacked a command that uses finger.exe to download malicious payloads from a remote domain.

hunt.name: Amazon ClickFix Finger Utility Abuse
hunt.description: Attackers use SEO poisoning to drive victims to a fake Amazon login page where a pastejacked command is copied to the clipboard. The command uses finger.exe to communicate with a remote server over port 79, retrieving a malicious script hidden within a .plan file. This hunt identifies the initial access and execution stages of a ClickFix campaign that uses the legacy finger.exe utility as a LOLbin. The hunt scopes for suspicious DNS resolutions to known campaign infrastructure, identifies obfuscated finger.exe executions, and uses a prevalence count to highlight rare command-line arguments across the environment.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{malicious_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify hosts resolving the initial lure or delivery domains associated with the BBQ-themed infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: A hostname resolving one of the reported domains. Silence indicates no interaction with the known infrastructure.

primitive_config.label: DNS resolutions to campaign domains
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, time FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{malicious_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A hostname resolving one of the reported domains. Silence indicates no interaction with the known infrastructure.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger.exe') AND (process_cmd_line LIKE '%@%' OR instr(process_cmd_line, '^') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, ',') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, '-') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, '_') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find finger executions that include an @ symbol for remote connections or command-line obfuscation characters used in this campaign.
config.expected_signal: A process row showing the finger utility targeting a remote user or using shell-escape characters. Silence is expected as finger is a legacy tool.

primitive_config.label: Obfuscated or remote finger execution
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger.exe') AND (process_cmd_line LIKE '%@%' OR instr(process_cmd_line, '^') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, ',') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, '-') > 0 OR instr(process_cmd_line, '_') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: A process row showing the finger utility targeting a remote user or using shell-escape characters. Silence is expected as finger is a legacy tool.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger.exe') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY cmd HAVING hosts <= 3
config.description: Stack-count finger command lines to identify rare or unique activity that deviates from standard administrative use.
config.expected_signal: Unique or rare finger commands that appear on only a few hosts. High counts likely indicate legacy scripts.

primitive_config.label: Rare finger command lines
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_cmd_line) AS cmd, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%finger.exe') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY cmd HAVING hosts <= 3
primitive_config.expected: Unique or rare finger commands that appear on only a few hosts. High counts likely indicate legacy scripts.

config.objective: Determine if a host resolving campaign DNS domains also executed a suspicious finger command. Explicitly verify that the DNS resolution to campaign domains occurred shortly before the finger execution on the same host, indicating a successful pastejacking attack.
